note.explanation: Glycogen is the main stored form of glucose. It is kept in the liver and muscles, where the body can use it as a source of glucose.
examples: Between meals, the body can use stored glycogen.
During exercise, the body can use glycogen stored in the muscles.
note.checkAnswer: Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose. It is stored in the liver and muscles.
note.simple: Glycogen is like a store of glucose that the body can use later.
note.checkQuestion: Where is glycogen stored, and what is its role?
note.title: Glycogen as the body's glucose store
steps: Food is digested and its molecules are absorbed by cells.
Glucose can be stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
The body can use this stored resource when it needs energy.
note.answer: Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose, stored in the liver and muscles.

written.text: Explain the role of lipids in our body.
written.finalAnswer: Lipids serve as an energy reserve within our body. About half of the fuel our body needs comes from lipids. Excess food is stored as lipids in adipose cells. Between meals and during exercise, our body relies on this resource to provide energy.

written.text:
Explain the following terms.  
Activation energy, Transition state, Aerobic respiration
written.finalAnswer: Activation energy: The energy needed by the reactant particles to change into the transition state. Transition state: The state formed when reactant particles collide before they change into products. Aerobic respiration: The process of respiration that occurs in the presence of oxygen.

example.question: Write the aerobic respiration reaction shown in your textbook.

explain.title: Aerobic respiration
explain.body: The process that occurs in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration. In the textbook's reaction, glucose is first split into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. The next stage uses oxygen and occurs in the mitochondria, producing carbon dioxide, water, and energy.

explain.title: Glycolysis and ATP
explain.body: During glycolysis one molecule of glucose is split into two molecules of pyruvate. This series of enzyme-catalysed reactions has a net production of 2 ATP. Cells use ATP and break it down when they need energy for metabolic activities.

explain.title: Anaerobic respiration
explain.body: In certain organisms like bacteria and algae respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and it is called anaerobic respiration. The section describes glucose being converted into carbon dioxide and ethanol with the evolution of energy.

explain.title: Lipids and glycogen
explain.body: Lipids serve as an energy reserve within our body; excess food can be stored as lipids in adipose cells. Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose and is stored in the liver and muscles.

mistakes: Do not confuse aerobic respiration, which occurs in the presence of oxygen, with anaerobic respiration, which occurs in its absence.
Do not say glycolysis produces 2 molecules of ATP; the textbook states that its net production is 2 ATP.
Do not give only the storage location when asked for glycogen's role; state that it is the primary storage form of glucose.
Do not describe lipids only as stored excess food; explain that they provide an energy reserve used between meals and during exercise.
